data.title: Sunscreens (avobenzone, oxybenzone, tinted sunscreens)
data.summary: XI Miscellaneous · Ultraviolet filters: organic (chemical) absorbers and inorganic (physical/mineral) blockers
data.body:
_Topicals · XI Miscellaneous_

**Class:** Ultraviolet filters: organic (chemical) absorbers and inorganic (physical/mineral) blockers

## Mechanism of action
- Organic filters absorb UV energy and release it as heat
- Avobenzone (butyl methoxydibenzoylmethane): the main UVA1 filter (320–400 nm, peak 357 nm); photo-unstable — needs stabilisers (octocrylene, bemotrizinol)
- Oxybenzone (benzophenone-3): absorbs UVB and UVA2 (broad, up to about 350 nm); the most common photoallergen; concerns about hormone effects and coral reefs
- Inorganic filters (zinc oxide, titanium dioxide) reflect, scatter and absorb UVB and UVA; zinc oxide covers UVA1 better
- Tinted sunscreens contain iron oxides → block visible light (blue light), which worsens melasma and PIH in skin types IV–VI

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Prevention of sunburn, photoageing, actinic keratoses, SCC (proven), melanoma and BCC (supportive data)
- Photodermatoses (PLE, lupus, porphyrias, chronic actinic dermatitis, XP)
- Melasma, PIH, vitiligo (prevent burning and contrast), patients on photosensitising drugs or after procedures

## Dose & formulations
- Broad spectrum, SPF 30 or more (SPF 50+ for photosensitive), UVA rating PA+++ or higher; tinted for melasma
- Amount: 2 mg/cm² (about ½ teaspoon for face and neck; ~30 mL — a 'shot glass' — for the whole adult body); most people apply only a quarter to half of this
- Apply 15–30 min before going out; reapply every 2 hours and after swimming or sweating
- SPF = ratio of MED with sunscreen to MED without (UVB); SPF 15 blocks ~93%, SPF 30 ~97%, SPF 50 ~98% of UVB
- UVA protection measures: PPD/PA rating, critical wavelength ≥370 nm

## Adverse effects
- Irritant dermatitis (stinging, especially around eyes)
- Allergic and photoallergic contact dermatitis (oxybenzone, octocrylene, PABA)
- Acne/comedones with oily formulations; white cast with inorganic filters
- Possible lower vitamin D synthesis (rarely clinically significant)

## Contraindications
- Known allergy to a filter; infants under 6 months — prefer shade and clothing; mineral sunscreen on small areas if needed

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe; mineral sunscreens preferred by some in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- Avobenzone = UVA1 filter but photo-unstable
- Oxybenzone = commonest photoallergen
- Iron oxide (tinted) protects against visible light — melasma
- SPF measures UVB; PA/PPD measures UVA; 2 mg/cm²

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.50 (Sunscreens); Khopkar ch.25. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
